newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO plunge into crisis over redeployment.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO plunge into crisis over redeployment.

text.p: Palestinians clashed with Israeli soldiers in the West Bank on Monday, deepening a crisis over an Israeli troop redeployment plan angrily rejected by Yasser Arafat as a trick.
Witnesses said some 150 Israeli soldiers used clubs and guns to beat back about 100 Palestinians who tried to stop workers from opening a road for Jewish settlers near the West Bank town of Hebron.

The clash was the first serious outbreak of Israeli-Arab violence since Palestinian President Arafat spurned an Israeli decision on Friday to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank to PLO rule.
Palestinians wanted 30 percent and a say in determining the scope of this and two other pullbacks from mainly rural areas of the West Bank mandated by Israel-PLO peace deals.

"It is a matter of Israeli implementation, not for Palestinian-Israeli negotiation, and the Palestinians were the first to admit this in their discussions with us," said Dore Gold, a senior adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"We do not seek a confrontation but if the Palestinian side chooses confrontation it will first of all be Palestinian interests that are hurt," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel Radio.
Naveh said Israel had "learned the lessons" of violence that erupted last September after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem.

Israeli security sources said the army has a plan to deploy tanks and snipers in the West Bank if clashes, such as those that killed 61 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers six months ago, break out again.

In a sign of growing Arab anger over Israel's redeployment plan, the chief Palestinian peace negotiator handed Arafat his resignation on Monday, PLO officials said. Arafat has yet to accept the decision by Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen.

"There is a real crisis because there is a clear breaching to what had been agreed upon," Arafat told reporters in Gaza, referring to the redeployment. He called the Israeli move "a trick and a conspiracy against the peace process".
Netanyahu flew to Russia on Monday for an official visit. Israel Radio quoted a senior official on board his plane as saying Israel and the PLO "appeared to be headed towards a difficult crisis".
The nine-percent decision followed two other actions that irked Palestinians -- approval for another Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem and steps to shut down four PLO offices there.
Foreign Minister David Levy said he made clear to Abu Mazen in talks on Sunday that Israel would not reconsider building the settlement nor negotiate the West Bank pullback.
But an Israeli official said Israel would not go ahead with the redeployment so long as the PLO, which currently has sole control of about three percent of the West Bank, rejected it.
Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo warned of a possible repetition of September's violence that almost destroyed the Israel-PLO peace process.
"The policy of Mr Netanyahu and his government will lead us to the abyss, will lead us to very dangerous things which we are all trying to avoid," Abed Rabbo told Israel Radio.
Naveh said the real problem was "unrealistic" Palestinian expectations: "They understand these expectations are unacceptable to the current Israeli government."
